content.text:
I've submitted index 12 (Co 0.53 / Sb 0.47) as the best composition. It was the only one of the three I measured with a positive EQE, but that result is still close to zero.

| Index | Composition (Co / Sb) | Why I measured it | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18 | 0.33 / 0.67 | CoSb2O6: the MACE model puts it on the stability hull (stable) | −0.0042 |
| 5 | 0.76 / 0.24 | Co7Sb2O12 spinel: close to stable, and MEGNet predicts a 1.44 eV band gap, low enough to absorb the 2.1 eV light | −0.0007 |
| 12 | 0.53 / 0.47 | Middle of the line, where the film is probably a mix of those two phases; the GP ranked this area as least certain | +0.0049 |

- **The result is weak.** All three values sit near the noise floor, so index 12 being best is not a clear win. The Co–Sb line may simply be a poor photoanode under this light.
- **Big gaps are untested.** With only three merit measurements, the Co-rich end (indices 0–4), 0.13–0.18 Sb, and the Sb-rich end (19–28, 0.71–0.86 Sb) were never measured.
- **The band-gap model was off.** MEGNet predicted only 0.37 eV for CoSb2O6, which I judged to be an underestimate. Its predicted gaps did not match the measurements: both compositions it suggested would absorb gave about zero.
- **No XRD was used.** None of the 5 XRD measurements were spent, so the "mixed-phase" reading of index 12 is an inference, not something I confirmed.
